request.description: Call any REST or GraphQL endpoint that Lodol has no built-in step for. Set the method, URL, headers, query parameters, and body, and the response comes back ready for later steps to read. Store an API token as a workspace secret and reference it in a header to make an authenticated call.
request.name: request

parameters.description: The full address to call, starting with https://. It can be built from workspace values, for example @values.BASE_URL followed by the path.
parameters.name: url

parameters.description: The HTTP method the endpoint expects.
parameters.name: method

parameters.description: Headers to send, such as an Authorization header. Use a workspace secret for a token so it is never stored in the workflow.
parameters.name: headers

parameters.description: Values added to the end of the URL as a query string. Anything already written into the URL is kept.
parameters.name: query

parameters.description: What to send with the request, as JSON or a reference to a value from an earlier step. Leave it empty for a request that carries no body, such as a GET.
parameters.name: body

parameters.description: How to encode the body. JSON suits most APIs, including GraphQL. Form sends it the way an HTML form would.
parameters.name: body_format

parameters.description: How to read what comes back. Auto follows the response's own content type, so JSON becomes an object and a download becomes a file.
parameters.name: response_format

parameters.description: What to do when the endpoint answers with an error status. Continuing lets later steps check the status themselves, which suits a 404 that just means not found.
parameters.name: on_error

description: Call any REST or GraphQL endpoint.
